card.name: Word after diminish/decrease the effect
card.fires_on: The word right after a drug-interaction phrase such as "diminish the antihypertensive" or "decrease the effect", mostly "effect" or "of", just before the affected drug is named.

modes.label: Effect before affected drug
modes.description: The word "effect" after "may diminish the antihypertensive", just before the drug whose action is reduced.

modes.label: Link word after effect
modes.description: "of" or a possessive after an effect or clearance noun, before the drug named.
modes.example: adiol, estrone, progesterone and other steroidal hormones: Pretreatment with or concurrent administration of phenobarbital may decrease the effect<< of>> estradiol by increasing its metabolism.

modes.label: Non-medical verb
modes.description: A rare general-text case, a verb after a noun in a descriptive sentence.
modes.example: and "Thou. " . . . The revolutionary posters were everywhere, flaming the walls in clean reds and blues that made the few remaining advertisements<< look>> like daubs of mud. . .
